cells.tense: Right now you are carrying something, and it is not changing your shape.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: When someone hands you the weight of their day, sit with it beside them and feel what it costs you while you listen. Stay with them and stay your own — not fused, not gone.
cells.core:
There is something on you and it is not bending you. That is the plain version of what is working: the weight is real, your outline is intact, and you are not white-knuckling to keep it that way. When you look at a hard thing and see its workings — where the pressure comes from, what would happen if it were set down — you bear it better than you did when you were only bracing. Seeing the shape of a load is not the same as taking it on. You can do the first without the second.

The next thing this can feed is other people. Not fixing them and not holding them up. Sitting with someone who is under something, letting their weight register on you while you keep your own side, is a small act with a clear edge. It keeps the work honest, because strength that only ever runs alone starts to think it is the only one in the building.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold this without losing your shape.
cells.verb: bearing what is laid on you without either breaking or turning to stone
cells.place: the bare shape of a thing, with the particular weight lifted off it

cells.tense: You will be braced for a pressure that has not arrived and may never arrive.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: When you catch yourself braced for something that is not here, look at what is actually on you today and bring the grip down to meet it. No more than that, and then stop.
cells.core:
Something in you is getting ready early. You are gripping before there is anything to grip, checking the strap before the strap has a job — and the bracing itself now costs what the weight would have. From inside it feels like strength. From outside the muscle is simply locked. What you are guarding is not in danger yet, and staying clenched until it is means you arrive at the real thing already worn down. The pattern you see so clearly — how it will go, what will be asked — is a forecast, not a fact. You read mechanism better than most, which is exactly why the forecast feels solid.

A way back is smaller than it sounds. Fairness here is not punishment and not reward. It is the grip matching the load.

cells.tense: Something came down on you and you have been standing at that door ever since.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Take what you have been holding since then — a version of events, a duty, a grudge — and release it on purpose. Sit with empty hands a while and notice what they do.
cells.core:
Something landed and you went down under it, and you have been braced for the next one since. That is why holding now looks like standing near an exit. From where you are standing the door is still open and something is still coming. It is not. You are clear about how pressure works — you can see the mechanism, the shape of a load, the way a thing gives — and that clarity has turned into a reason not to pick anything up at all. Knowing how a thing collapses is not the same as knowing it will. The strength you cannot locate has not gone anywhere; it is set down while you watch the door.

Put down the grip, not the load. There is a specific thing you have been holding past the point it needed holding, and letting go of it once is small enough to try today.
cells.sheetLine: Holding anything feels dangerous since then.

cells.tense: You are already doing the thing you say you cannot do.
cells.act: remember what drew you and face it again
cells.ask: Think of the last thing you were drawn toward before you decided it wasn't for you, and give it honest attention again — not to act on it, just to look at what pulled you.
cells.core:
There is strength in this account and a collapse in this account, and neither is filed under your name. You would say you are just getting through. Meanwhile you are the person holding the shape while others come apart in it, and the person who goes flat for a week and calls it tired. Both are you. The pattern is right there and you keep reading it as conditions. What you see so clearly in how things work, you do not turn on yourself — your own case gets described from the outside. That is not modesty. It is a blind spot with good manners.

What you want is a better clue than what you are enduring. There was something you were drawn to before you ruled it out. Face it again — not to act on it, just to look plainly. The pull is yours, and nobody made it for you.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is carrying weight for others or has recently been crushed by a load — the record gives a capacity and its failure modes, not a history, so every cell must stay on the mechanism and let them place it. A reader could reasonably say 'nothing is pressing on me right now', which is why each core names what the capacity does in a moment they could recognise rather than asserting a situation. The asks survive that being wrong: they are all small acts of the person's own, doable whether or not my read lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that congratulates the endurance itself — 'you were built to hold more than most' — so that praise is cut and the cells stay on what holding is doing now.
